newsitem.title: UK: Anglo offers to cut Lonrho stake - FT.
newsitem.headline: Anglo offers to cut Lonrho stake - FT.

text.p: South African mining giant Anglo American Corp has offered to drop its increased stake in Britain's Lonrho Plc to nine percent, following objections from the European Commission (EC), the Financial Times said on Friday.

The South African firm increased its stake from 10 percent to 28.4 percent six months ago but immediately ran into opposition from EC competition commissioner Karel Van Miert, who said it would jeopardise competition in the world's platinum market.
"Under the terms of the deal (with the EC), Anglo will divest all but nine percent of its shares in Lonrho," the Financial Times said.
It said the rest would have to be put in the hands of a trustee and sold off within two years to third parties.
"This commitment will allow the Commission to say 'yes'," the paper quoted an unnamed official as saying.
"Anglo maintained quite a hard position right up until the end but when they saw that the Commission did not blink they realised they had to change their offer," the official said.

European Union officials and industry sources had said on Thursday they expected the EC to force Anglo to cut its stake, because the deal would effectively put the world's platinum market under the control of Anglo and its compatriot Gencor Ltd .
The EC blocked Lonrho and Gencor merging their platinum interests last year.

The sources had told Reuters that Anglo was still actively negotiating but it was thought it would have to reduce its stake to nine or 10 percent, and it was predicted the excess would have to be sold off via a trust.
